subject: Scope alignment: SOC 2 coverage window, bridge confirmation, and renewal evidence checklist
messages:
From: Lindsey Park <lindsey@veridia.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewals: SOC 2 Type II and procurement checklist

Hi Hannah,

We're starting our renewal packet for Veridia's ML platform contracts and need to confirm Redwood's SOC 2 Type II coverage and any available bridge documentation. Procurement asked specifically for: 

- Latest SOC 2 Type II report (audit period)
- Any bridge letter that covers the interval between the report end date and the renewal effective date
- A short evidence checklist for the procurement team (which control families have external validations vs. internal attestations)

Our renewal target date is 2026-12-15 and procurement wants to know whether a bridge will cover the gap until the next Type II release. Can you confirm the audit period (start/end) and whether Redwood can provide a bridge letter if the new Type II isn't issued before our renewal?

I can loop in our security and procurement contacts if helpful.

Thanks,
Lindsey Park
Head of Procurement, Veridia Inc.
procurement@veridia.com

---
Attachment: (none)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Lindsey Park <lindsey@veridia.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewals: SOC 2 Type II and procurement checklist

Hi Lindsey — thanks for the note and timeline. I'm copying Neha (security) and Sergio (account lead) so we can give a complete response. Quick answers up front:

- We can provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report and a standard bridge letter if required.
- Our most recent Type II report covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (I'll attach it once Neha confirms).
- We can produce a short procurement evidence checklist that maps high-level control families to available artifacts (logs, policy docs, evidence bundles).

Neha — can you attach the PDF of the Type II and a draft bridge letter (if available)? Also please flag any control families that currently have partial evidence only and estimate turnaround for full artifacts. Sergio — I'm happy to schedule a quick 20-minute sync with Veridia procurement this week if that helps finalize dates.

Lindsey — would a bridge letter that covers 2026-10-01 through the new report publication date work for procurement, or do you need the bridge to start on the renewal effective date (2026-12-15)? Let me know the preferred coverage window.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0132

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Lindsey Park <lindsey@veridia.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewals: SOC 2 Type II and procurement checklist

Hi all — attaching the report and draft bridge letter for review. Summary below:

- SOC 2 Type II report: audit period 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (attached PDF).
- Draft bridge letter: covers 2026-10-01 through 2027-01-15 or until next Type II is issued (whichever comes first). We can narrow the end date to match Veridia's renewal effective date (2026-12-15) if you prefer.
- Procurement evidence checklist: attached spreadsheet lists the common artifacts we can deliver on 3 business-day notice (logs, configuration screenshots, policy docs) and items that require additional redaction or legal review (penetration-test reports, customer-specific audit artifacts).

Notes / caveats:
- Pen test reports and some vendor contracts require execution of a mutual NDA or a short disclosure addendum; we can provide redacted summaries without an NDA.
- Bridge letters are signed by our Head of Security and describe the coverage scope; they do not replace the formal Type II report but are accepted by some procurement teams for renewal SOWs.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-10-01_2026-09-30.pdf, SOC2_Bridge_Letter_20261031.pdf, procurement_evidence_checklist.xlsx

If Veridia needs the bridge to start on 2026-12-15 specifically, confirm and we'll update the draft wording. If you need DocuSign for an NDA, reply and I'll generate a link.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

From: Lindsey Park <lindsey@veridia.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T16:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Renewals: SOC 2 Type II and procurement checklist

Thanks, Neha — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple clarifications from procurement/security: 

1) Coverage window: For contract continuity, procurement prefers the bridge to explicitly cover the renewal effective date (2026-12-15) through the issuance of the next Type II. Can you update the draft to start 2026-12-15?
2) Evidence checklist: please highlight which artifacts are available immediately vs. those that need an NDA or redaction. The spreadsheet looks good but we need the immediate-availability column filled out where possible.
3) Signature authority: who will sign the bridge letter? Procurement requires the signer to be the Head of Security or equivalent (name/title).

Timing: procurement needs confirmation no later than 2026-11-04 to include in the renewal packet. If possible, please provide the updated bridge wording and the immediate-availability columns filled in before then.

Lindsey Park
Head of Procurement, Veridia Inc.
procurement@veridia.com
Phone: +1 646-555-4452

- Neha/Laura: populate "immediate availability" column in procurement_evidence_checklist.xlsx and mark items that require NDA/redaction. Deliver spreadsheet by 2026-11-03 EOD.
- Hannah/Sergio: schedule a 20-min sync with Veridia procurement (Hannah to propose time slots).

Lindsey — if you can confirm the single preferred renewal effective date for wording (2026-12-15), we will use that as the bridge start. Otherwise we'll include both options (start on 2026-10-01 or 2026-12-15) with procurement preference called out.

Thanks — we'll circle back with the updated artifacts and the DocuSign link.
